title: VEG-03A — Microbiological and Nutritional Analysis of Lettuce Crops
plainFinding: Researchers found no harmful human germs in the tested lettuce, supporting its use as fresh food for astronauts.
caveat: The paper discusses three lettuce plantings (VEG-01A, VEG-01B and VEG-03A). Its no-pathogen conclusion is reported across the tested plantings; do not imply that every possible contaminant was tested.

title: VEG-03D — Spatial Characterization of Microbial Communities on Leafy Greens
plainFinding: Food-safety checks found none of three harmful germs they screened for in leafy greens grown during VEG-03D, 03E and 03F.
caveat: The paper reports the food-safety screening across the related VEG-03D, 03E and 03F runs. It reports negative screening for E. coli, S. aureus and Salmonella; this is not a guarantee that food is free of every germ.

title: Inspiration4 — Molecular and Physiological Changes in Civilian Crew
plainFinding: After the three-day flight, almost all measured health markers were similar to the crew's pre-flight levels.
caveat: Only four people took part, and the study had no age- and sex-matched Earth control group. The authors describe these early civilian-flight findings as preliminary; they do not prove that long Moon or Mars missions are safe.

title: ALTEA-Survey — Space Station US Laboratory Radiation Detector
plainFinding: A radiation detector aboard the space station recorded dose-equivalent readings in the US Laboratory.
caveat: This is an archived ISS measurement, not a Moon or Mars reading. The selected measurement is dose equivalent; it should not be treated as a direct prediction for another location.

title: ALTEA Space Station Radiation Survey (Narici et al. 2015)
plainFinding: Published measurements found average radiation rates between 0.10 and 0.52 mSv per day aboard the space station.
caveat: Protons only partly counted. Published research (Narici et al. 2015). Low-Earth orbit reading inside heavy shielding, never on the same axis as Moon or Mars surface values.
